market_summary: Markets are experiencing a severe selloff today with SPY down 4.41%, QQQ plunging 6.49%, and NVDA cratering 9.26% as tech leads the decline. The VIX has spiked to 28.18 reflecting elevated fear, while inverse/volatility products surge with SQQQ up 19.23% and UVIX soaring 61.16% today. Healthcare and Financials are the relative outperformers but still down 2.5% and 2.87% respectively, indicating broad-based selling pressure.
key_insight: The semiconductor sector is getting crushed on data-center optimism concerns post-election — watch whether NVDA and chip names find support or if the selling accelerates into next week, as AMAT earnings on 11/12 could be a catalyst for the group.
sentiment_commentary: The Fear & Greed Index at 28 confirms deep fear positioning, which historically can precede short-term bounces but in the context of a 4%+ SPY selloff, suggests panic selling may not be complete. Elevated VIX at 28.18 means options premiums are expensive, favoring directional equity plays over options strategies for swing trades.
notable_movers: NVDA is the biggest watchlist loser today at -9.26%, underperforming even the already-weak QQQ by nearly 3 percentage points. SQQQ surged 19.23% today, continuing its pattern as our highest-conviction repeat winner with a +19.40% closed trade just recently. MSFT dropped 3.58% today giving back last week's gains, while BTC-USD is flat at +0.07%, showing unusual resilience versus equities.
macro_context: The 10-Year Treasury yield at 4.9% is putting significant pressure on growth stocks, with the positive yield curve spread of 0.32% suggesting the market is pricing in sustained higher rates. GDP growth remains strong at 3.4% but the Fed Funds rate at 3.88% with unemployment at 4.2% suggests the Fed has limited room to ease, keeping the pressure on equity valuations. Post-midterm election dynamics and political uncertainty are adding to volatility.

swing_trades.thesis: SQQQ is our highest conviction repeat winner (+19.40% and +8.11% on prior closed trades). With XLK down 8% today leading the selloff, tech weakness looks poised to continue into next week as semiconductor concerns (Micron, ARM headlines) and elevated Treasury yields at 4.9% pressure growth multiples. SQQQ benefits directly from QQQ's -6.49% today and momentum selling typically extends 2-3 sessions after moves of this magnitude.
swing_trades.invalidation: Setup is invalid if QQQ reclaims above $680 indicating a sharp reversal, which would push SQQQ below $44.

swing_trades.thesis: SOXS surged 39.22% today on 1.6x average volume, outperforming SPY by 43.63%, as semiconductor stocks are the epicenter of this selloff on data-center optimism concerns. RSI at 75.1 is overbought but in strong momentum-driven inverse ETFs, overbought readings often persist. AMAT earnings on 11/12 could provide another catalyst for chip weakness. The unusual volume flagged here signals high conviction institutional positioning against semiconductors.
swing_trades.invalidation: Setup fails if semiconductor stocks stage a sharp recovery pushing SOXS below $70, negating the bearish-on-chips thesis.

swing_trades.thesis: SLV is only down 0.49% today versus SPY's -4.41%, showing exceptional relative strength during a broad market selloff. Gold above $4,000 per headlines confirms precious metals are benefiting from political uncertainty and elevated fear. With VIX at 28 and F&G at 28, safe-haven flows should continue. Despite our prior SLV loss, the setup is different now — entering during a flight-to-safety selloff rather than chasing momentum.
swing_trades.invalidation: Invalid if risk-on sentiment returns sharply and SLV breaks below $44, suggesting metals are losing safe-haven bid.
